messages:
perf-ci-bot: ALERT: ap-syd-l4 nightly perf-run shows regression after merge. p95 ~1.1s -> 2.4s, p99 ~2.8s -> 6.7s. Suspect recent batch/kselector changes. CI run: https://ci.redwood-inference/internal/1487 :eyes:

morgan: ugh, saw a couple of customer reports in the morning. Canary showed weird tail latency on L4 in ap-syd. Is this the PR that landed last night? @sanjay? :thinking_face:

sanjay: PR 5239 (batch-weighting + kselector tweak) landed at 02:12 UTC. I can start a quick bisect across canaries.

laura: posting two quick artifacts: flame graph from a noisy instance and the kselector decision log. Link: https://s3.redwood-inference/perf/artifacts/5239-ap-syd-flame.svg

laura: flame shows a bump in time spent in kselector_v2::choose_kernel and also more frequent kvcache evict ops. Not typical for pure batch logic.

nate: checked NIC/host counters on the canary: rx_packets steady but rx_dropped + rx_crc_errors spiked on the same hosts during the tests. rx_ring utilization high, netdev tx queue never saturates. Could be packet coalescing changes interacting with the kernel selector's affinity.

morgan: can you paste the netstat / ethtool snapshot?

nate: sure, here's the short output from the worst host (host-az3-14):

```
$ ethtool -S eth0 | egrep "rx_|tx_"
rx_packets: 12345678
rx_dropped: 8421
rx_crc_errors: 0
tx_packets: 9876543
tx_dropped: 12
rx_ring_full: 421
```

laura: also dumping runtime logs for kernel selector: found repeated fallback to CPU fallback kernel when L4 kernel probe timed out. snippet: `kselector: probe_timeout(200ms) -> fallback_cpu`, repeated many times. That increases CPU work per request and triggers more KV cache churn.

sanjay: started automated bisect against merges. Quick note: reverting only the kselector change (PR 5239/part-A) or the batching weight change (part-B) separately might isolate. Running two revert candidates now.

perf-ci-bot: Bisect results: revert of kselector tweak (revert commit abcdef1234) returns p99 close to baseline (6.7s -> 2.9s). Revert of batch-weighting alone shows smaller improvement (6.7s -> 5.8s).

morgan: that's pretty conclusive. kselector change seems primary. Any idea why NIC errors correlate? Could be timing path changes causing small packets to be more sensitive to driver coalescing?

nate: hypothesis: kselector_v2 probes kernels more aggressively, causing short-lived high-frequency small UDP/TCP packets as we probe telemetry endpoints, which trips NIC rx ring thresholds under older driver on L4 machines. We haven't seen this on A10/H100 clusters because their kernel probe code path uses a different timing window.

laura: I dug into the code: we reduced probe timeout and increased parallel kernel probes to improve cold-start latency. That reduces average latency but increases concurrent kernel introspection work. On L4 infra, that introspection path shares a polling thread that touches KV cache metadata; with the driver oddities it causes disk-backed evictions to spike.

sanjay: propose immediate action: hold rollout (abort remaining canaries), revert kselector tweak in staging and trigger full canary cycle, open follow-up to implement adaptive probe backoff for L4/older NIC drivers.

morgan: agree. @deploy-bot can you revert the commit in prod canary groups and pin rolling?

deploy-bot: Received revert request. Executing: `git revert abcdef1234 && ./scripts/deploy --groups=ap-syd-l4 --strategy=canary --reason="revert kselector tweak after perf regression"`

deploy-bot: Revert completed on canary group (ap-syd-l4). Monitoring: starting new perf-run.

perf-ci-bot: Post-revert perf-run: p95 1.2s, p99 3.0s. Close to baseline.

morgan: good. Hold the rollout for the global merge. We'll open an action item to: 1) increase probe timeout for L4 hosts, 2) add driver-detection heuristic to avoid parallel probes on NICs with rx_ring signals, 3) add a KV cache metric guard to abort heavy eviction patterns.

laura: I'll file the follow-up RFC and a test harness to simulate rx_ring pressure in CI.

sanjay: adding tests to the merge gate to run a lightweight canary on L4-sized instances before global rollout. Also tagging PR-5239 as blocked until adaptive backoff is implemented.

morgan: thanks all. Summary: rollouts paused, kselector tweak reverted in ap-syd-l4 canary, root cause likely aggressive kernel probes + NIC rx_ring sensitivity causing KV cache thrash. Follow-ups assigned. :white_check_mark:
